items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Another great musician I saw at Keith was a clarinettist by the name of Wilton Crawley.

ctx.x: which had had theatres in most large cities in the United States. It was at this theatre that I saw Bill "Bojangles" Robinson who was a great tap dancer. "Bojangles" would stand almost perfectly still and his feet be tapping rhythms that many drummers could not imitate on their snare drums.

Another great musician I saw at Keith was a clarinettist by the name of Wilton Crawley. Crawley would put a glass of water on his forhead and do a slow summersault while playing his clarinet and never spill a drop of water from the glass. I also saw Rudy Weidoft who was known as the fastest executor on an alto saxophone in those times. There were also classical pianists that came to Keith's Theatre and one I remember had two very long grand pianos, one which was controlled by electricity and he played a…

There was a man living next door to me named Mr. Thompson who played trumpet and baritone horn in a band lead by Mr. Bert Ferguson who played trumpet. Mr. Ferguson came to Cincinnati around 1917 and formed a marching and concert band for the Knights of Pythians lodge. I used to clean and polish Mr. Thompson's horn for which he would pay me for doing it.
